title: "What is the minimum trimmed sink rate when bounded below the section stall angle?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 480.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 900.0      # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 19.9      # s the probe actually used

res = optimize_geometry_for_sink_rate(get_airplane, alpha_max=6.7)

stall_angle = 6.7
prev_sink = 0.60 # from 2026-09-29-01-how-low-can-trimmed-sink-rate-be-driven-with-free-geometry-without-cos.qmd

sink = res['sink']
v_trim = res['v_trim']
alpha = res['alpha_trim']
le_sweep = res['le_sweep']
wing_x_le = res['wing_x_le']
wing_inc = res['wing_inc']
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{sink:.2f} m/s"`]{.hero-value}
[trimmed sink rate]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Constraining the trim angle of attack to the realistic stall angle of [`{python} f"{stall_angle:.1f}"`]{.key} degrees limits the achievable sink rate to [`{python} f"{sink:.2f} m/s"`]{.key} at [`{python} f"{v_trim:.2f} m/s"`]{.key}. Without this bound, the optimizer had achieved [[`{python} f"{prev_sink:.2f} m/s"`]{.key}](2026-09-29-01-how-low-can-trimmed-sink-rate-be-driven-with-free-geometry-without-cos.qmd) by trimming well past stall, exploiting the naive inviscid lift curve. The bounded optimal configuration sweeps the wings to [`{python} f"{le_sweep:.1f}°"`]{.key}.
